items.title: Ernie Cagnolatti Interview, 1961-04-05
items.q: Did he ever stress that in his lessons? ... he didn't actually stress to me about the non-pressure system of playing. Even when he started me on double-tonging and triple-tonging, he wanted me to use...

ctx.x: But Manetta... No, it didn't. It was one down and one up. In other words, you made two beats. Now, four concerts started making one out, two, three, four. It was one, two, three, four. You see? You count two down and two up.

That was your four. I've heard that Arnaud Mottwey was famous for his non-pressure playing. He could walk up to a trumpet like hanging on a string and lower things like that. You could do that. Did he ever stress that in his lessons? That was not for you, not the first measure? Did he do anything special to teach you that?

Well, no. He didn't actually stress to me about the non-pressure system of playing. Even when he started me on double-tonging and triple-tonging, he wanted me to use... By me being so young, he wanted me to build the muscles up in my lips. See, that was the general idea. The non-pressure system, you don't use much muscles, you see. And he wanted me to build the muscles up in my lips. So he wanted me to play the natural way. Which he could play both ways, you understand? Yeah. But he mostly used the non-pressure…
